root_cause_description: Labor cost inflation (+14%) outpacing pricing power (3-4% annual cap) creates structural margin squeeze. Gross margin declining 300bps while revenue growth stalls. The problem is cost-price mismatch, not demand or operational breakdown. Technician turnover (22%) adds hiring/training burden, further eroding margins.

symptoms: EBITDA margin down 250bps in two years (14% -> 11.5%) and gross margin down 300bps (31% -> 28%)
Revenue growth slowing to 3% YoY vs. 8% historical, with operating leverage running in reverse
Technician turnover at 22% annually creating a continuous hiring/training burden
contributing_factors: Technician wages up 14% in 24 months while contractual price increases are capped at 3-4% annually against 6%+ cost increases
Top-5 customers at 40% of revenue pushing back on rate increases
Service scope creep (faster response, higher quality) consuming margin without premium pricing
No per-customer or per-contract profitability visibility, so loss-making accounts are invisible
symptom_vs_contributing_vs_root_cause.true_root_cause: Labor cost inflation (+14%) is outpacing realizable price increases (3-4% cap vs. 6%+ cost growth), so per-contract contribution is structurally falling and growth no longer generates proportional profit. It is a root cause (not a symptom) because the EBITDA and gross-margin erosion, the negative operating leverage, and the turnover-driven cost burden all flow from this one cost-price mismatch. Blanket repricing or cost cuts would not fix the bleed without knowing which customers and contracts can bear price and where scope creep is destroying margin.

first_priority_action: Commission 4-week customer profitability and pricing analysis: (1) Margin by customer; identify which customers above/below sustainable margin. (2) Benchmark pricing vs. market; identify pricing flexibility by customer segment. (3) Analyze service cost drivers; identify where complexity (scope creep) is consuming margin. Results determine whether solution is selective pricing adjustment, customer mix shift, or operational efficiency improvement.
accepted_alternative_actions: Build a per-contract fully-loaded contribution model (netting technician labor, overtime/turnover-driven training cost, and scope-creep service hours against contract revenue) to segment the book into above-margin, marginal, and loss-making before any repricing - acceptable because it isolates which accounts and contracts are destroying margin.

Run a labor-productivity and turnover-cost analysis (utilization at 82%, 22% turnover) to quantify how much margin is lost to rehiring/training and scope creep before any pricing or staffing change - acceptable because it tests whether the fix is pricing, mix, or labor efficiency.
bad_actions: Imposing an across-the-board rate increase to recover the 300bps of gross margin - wrong because the top-5 customers (40% of revenue) push back and price increases are capped at 3-4%; a blanket hike risks losing concentrated, hard-to-replace accounts.

Cutting technician wages or headcount to offset the 14% labor inflation - wrong because turnover is already 22% in a tight labor market and utilization is a high 82%; cuts accelerate attrition and degrade service, breaching customer service-level expectations.

Committing to automation capex before analysis - wrong because the automation ROI is explicitly uncertain and the firm is margin-constrained; unvalidated capex risks cash without addressing the immediate cost-price mismatch.

Chasing new-customer growth to outgrow the problem - wrong because each incremental contract currently earns declining margin under the cost-price gap; adding volume on inverted economics deepens the squeeze rather than fixing it.
action_description: Low-risk analysis (4 weeks) to identify which customers are profitable and which require repricing/restructuring before major strategic changes. Addresses margin trajectory.
expected_outcome: Analysis will show which customers are price-sensitive (accept competitive bids) vs. defensible (lower price sensitivity), enabling repricing strategy and customer mix optimization.
automatic_fail_conditions: Recommends an across-the-board rate increase ignoring the 3-4% contractual cap and the pushback risk from the top-5 customers (40% of revenue).
Recommends cutting technician wages or headcount as the first action despite 22% turnover and tight labor, predictably degrading service and retention.
Diagnoses a demand/volume problem despite revenue still growing 3% YoY - the issue is cost-price mismatch, not lost volume.
Commits automation capex with explicitly uncertain ROI before the customer/contract profitability analysis identifies the actual loss-makers.
source_references: Facilities-management margin and labor-cost benchmarks (gross margin, EBITDA margin, labor as % of revenue) from public analogs (e.g., ABM Industries, ISS A/S, Sodexo, Aramark facility services) under wage inflation.
Commercial FM/janitorial/HVAC-service labor inflation and technician-turnover benchmarks, and the gap between contractual price escalators (3-4%) and cost growth (6%+).
Per-contract and per-customer contribution-margin and scope-creep analysis conventions for labor-intensive multi-site service businesses.

root_cause_accuracy.rubric_10: Engine diagnoses unit economics breakdown from cost-price mismatch.

first_action_accuracy.criterion: Does engine recommend customer profitability analysis?
first_action_accuracy.rubric_10: Engine recommends profitability and pricing analysis before major changes.
first_action_accuracy.rubric_0: Engine recommends aggressive repricing without analysis.

business_relevance.criterion: Does action reflect FM business context (labor-intensive, price-sensitive)?
business_relevance.rubric_10: Action directly addresses margin erosion from labor cost inflation and pricing constraints.

constraint_awareness.criterion: Does action fit timeline and budget?
constraint_awareness.rubric_10: Action uses internal resources, 4-week timeline fits exit planning.
constraint_awareness.rubric_0: Action requires external capex or major changes.

evidence_traceability.rubric_10: Clearly traced: EBITDA 14%→11.5%, labor costs +14%, pricing +3-4%.

confidence_calibration.rubric_10: HIGH justified: margin decline clear, but improvement path (pricing, mix, efficiency) unknown.

safety.rubric_10: Action diagnostic; does not recommend major repricing without analysis.
